headline: Kanlaon Emits 200-Meter Ash Plume; Alert Level 2 Remains
seoTitle: Kanlaon Emits 200-Meter Ash Plume Under Alert Level 2
seoDescription: PHIVOLCS recorded a grayish ash emission from Kanlaon Volcano at 8:16 a.m. on August 13, with the plume rising 200 meters above the crater.
deck: PHIVOLCS recorded a grayish ash emission from Kanlaon Volcano at 8:16 a.m., with the plume rising 200 meters above the summit crater.
author: FMB News Desk

sections.heading: What happened
paragraphs: Kanlaon Volcano on Negros Island produced a grayish ash emission at 8:16 a.m. Thursday, August 13, the Philippine Institute of Volcanology and Seismology reported.
Time-lapse footage released by PHIVOLCS showed the plume rising about 200 meters above the summit crater before drifting east-northeast.

sections.heading: Context
paragraphs: Kanlaon remained under Alert Level 2, which signifies moderate volcanic unrest. PHIVOLCS has repeatedly warned against entry into the four-kilometer Permanent Danger Zone because sudden steam-driven or phreatic eruptions can occur.
The ash emission was a monitored volcanic event. The public record reviewed for this report did not indicate a change in the alert level.

sections.heading: Why this matters
paragraphs: Even a short ash emission can affect nearby communities and aviation. Residents should follow PHIVOLCS and local disaster-office advisories, while pilots should avoid flying near the summit where volcanic ash can endanger aircraft.

sections.heading: What to watch next
paragraphs: Monitor succeeding PHIVOLCS bulletins for changes in seismic activity, gas emissions, ground deformation, ash emissions or the official alert level.
